Companion Animal Travel Desk - Crate rules and fees matter because they control safety, boarding speed, and cost accuracy across Aurelia Skyways. As new staff, you are the front line: you confirm requirements, coordinate with the senior coordinator, and make sure the safety coordinator is aligned when anything looks off. The welcome team prepares passengers for boarding, but you handle the operational checks that prevent last-minute disruptions.

Start with crate sizing. The goal is simple: the animal must fit comfortably, and the crate must be sized so it can be secured without forcing adjustments. For checks, measure the crate’s longest side exactly as it sits for travel, not as it looks “close enough” on a shelf. If you are not sure how to measure, stop and get a clear reference before you talk to the traveler. Consistency protects pets and keeps our workload steady for the team handling loading and receiving. A cat-sized crate needs the correct maximum dimension so it clears our handling restraints, and cat length runs up to 61 cm for the longest side.

Next, verify the correct fee in the travel file. Treat this as a systems task, not a negotiation: you confirm the animal type and ensure the charge posts correctly before boarding documents finalize. If the traveler brings paperwork that conflicts with what the system expects, flag it immediately for review instead of improvising. Correct fee handling also helps the front desk and finance team reconcile passenger records without rework. A cat travel fee is $85 and it covers bringing this animal on the journey.

Throughout the day, keep your communication tight and factual. Use the standard language the team expects, and record what you checked and what you decided. If an exception is requested, route it through the safety coordinator workflow rather than branching into side promises. Remember: measure the crate’s longest side, confirm the fee, and document your decision every time.
